[Figure 1]

In the figure above, lines $s$ and $t$ are parallel. What is the value of $v$?
explanation: Choice C is correct. Because lines $s$ and $t$ are parallel, the angle marked $145 ^\circ$ and the leftmost angle marked $u ^\circ$ are same-side interior angles and therefore supplementary. Thus $145 ^\circ + u ^\circ = 180 ^\circ$, which yields $u = 35$. Lines $r$ and $s$ intersect at a right angle, so lines $p$, $r$, and $s$ form a right triangle whose two acute angles are $u ^\circ$ and $v ^\circ$. The acute angles of a right triangle are complementary, so $u ^\circ + v ^\circ = 90 ^\circ$. Substituting $u = 35$ yields $35 ^\circ + v ^\circ = 90 ^\circ$, and $v = 55$.
